suggested_titles.academic: Structural Isomorphism Registry: Cross-Domain Mappings in Theophysics
suggested_titles.provocative: Where Physics Meets Theology: A Registry of Structural Isomorphisms

opening_analysis.diagnosis: The opening is clear and functional but lacks a hook. It defines the registry immediately, which is efficient for a reference document but does not draw in a reader unfamiliar with the concept. The thesis (what the registry is) is visible in paragraph 1, but the problem it solves (why this registry matters) is not stated until later, if at all.

flow.suggested_reorder: No reordering needed; the document is a reference list with clear sections.

paragraph_function_map.main_point: This document is a registry of structural isomorphism records in the Theophysics framework.
Each record includes mapping, swap test, predictions, falsification criteria, and classification.
All records are evaluated against the Four-Test Protocol.
The Four-Test Protocol consists of Prediction Constraint, Symmetric Breaking, Connection Density, and Falsifiability Invitation.
A link to the full protocol document is provided.
The current registry table lists IDs, domains, status, confidence, and type.
A visual registry is available as an HTML file.
Instructions for adding a new record are provided.
Steps for adding a new record: copy template, name file, fill fields, update README, add to HTML.
Rules: falsifiability required, 'Analogy Only' is honest, swap test mandatory, observation precedes explanation.

rearrangement_suggestions: Consider moving the 'Rules' section (paragraph 10) before the 'How to Add' section for logical ordering.
Add a brief 'Why This Matters' paragraph after the definition to hook readers.
top_3_fixes: Add a hook paragraph explaining the significance of structural isomorphisms to motivate the registry.
Include a brief summary of the Four-Test Protocol inline rather than relying solely on a link.
Reorder sections so that rules precede instructions for adding records.
